methodology_notes: Observed Cmax reported as mean ± SD when primary source uses arithmetic statistics; as geometric mean with 90% CI in notes when that is the primary-source convention. SD field is null for geometric-mean-only sources. 2026-04-22 seed expansion (commit pending): added paclitaxel, docetaxel, micafungin, benzylpenicillin, torsemide (5 OATP1B1 substrates). benzylpenicillin classified as iv_infusion duration 4 min (rather than iv_bolus) because the FDA label's 3-5 min push is physically a short zero-order input; V3.1 infusion path handles it correctly and matches the Cmax timing (400 mg/L at 5-6 min post-start). 2026-04-22 second expansion: added vimseltinib, nerandomilast, balcinrenone, tolebrutinib, zibotentan (5 non-OATP1B1 oral drugs). Cmax in nmol/L converted to mg/L using MW from PubChem: nerandomilast MW=449.0 g/mol (710 nmol/L x 449.0/1000 = 0.3188 mg/L); balcinrenone MW=399.4 g/mol (4602 nmol/L x 399.4/1000 = 1.838 mg/L). 2026-04-23 third expansion: added sulopenem, ensitrelvir, elafibranor, obicetrapib, mirdametinib (5 non-OATP1B1 oral drugs, mechanism-diverse: penem antibiotic + OAT3 substrate, oral 3CL antiviral, dual PPAR agonist, CETP inhibitor, MEK1/2 inhibitor). All Cmax values cross-validated against DailyMed (FDA labels) or PMC primary papers. Sulopenem/ensitrelvir doses reported as labeled-salt mass; Cmax is for active species. Mirdametinib dose 4 mg maps to BSA 1.85 m² via GOMEKLI Table 1 (≥1.50 m² band), Cmax is steady-state per label Table 6. 2026-04-23 fourth expansion (18→22): added cefiderocol (IV, renal-cleared siderophore cephalosporin), eravacycline (IV, biliary-excretion fluorocycline), ampreloxetine (oral, CNS-BBB NRI, CYP1A2-primary), sepiapterin (oral, BH4 prodrug low-parent-Cmax regime). All 4 HV single-dose Phase 1 primary papers; PubChem InChIKey match with stereochemistry confirmed. Xanomeline candidate dropped from this chunk — FDA Integrated Review URL 404, Cobenfy DailyMed label has only steady-state Cmax. 2026-04-23 fifth expansion (22→26): added ulotaront (oral, TAAR1/5-HT1A agonist first-in-class antipsychotic + CYP2D6 fm=0.53), oliceridine (IV bolus, G-protein-biased mu-opioid + CYP3A4/CYP2D6), pitolisant (oral, H3 inverse agonist + CYP2D6-dominant), remdesivir (IV, phosphoramidate nucleotide prodrug + CES1/CYP3A4; 2020 NME). Fills CYP2D6-dominant metabolism class (previously empty) with 3 mechanistically-distinct drugs, opioid class (previously empty) with 1 drug, and adds 2020-era IV NME. All 4 single-dose HV PMC open-access; InChIKey full match incl. stereo for all (no SMILES substitution needed). Xanomeline re-attempt remains deferred. 2026-04-23 sixth expansion (26→30): added asundexian (oral FXIa inhibitor, CES1-primary metabolism; BAY 2433334 Phase 1 Day 1 data from Kubitza 2022 JTH), orforglipron (oral non-peptide GLP-1 agonist, MW 883 > 800 AD threshold; Yamada 2024 food-effect SAD fasted 3 mg), lorundrostat (oral aldosterone synthase CYP11B2 inhibitor; Shimizu 2024 CTS FIH-SAD 100 mg arm N=6), fexuprazan (oral PCAB + multi-CYP substrate; Kim 2023 Pharmaceuticals bioequivalence single-dose 40 mg reference arm). Fills CES1-primary metabolism, oral peptide-mimetic, aldosterone synthase, and PCAB classes (all previously empty). Asundexian Day 1 row used (Table 4) -- paper is MAD but Day 1 is true first-dose measurement. Fexuprazan is South-Korea-approved 2022 (pre-2024 era) but mechanism-unique. All 4 InChIKey full match incl. stereo against PubChem; URLs verified HTTP 200; table_refs verified verbatim via PMC WebFetch. 2026-04-23 seventh expansion (30→33): added lurbinectedin (IV 2020 NME Zepzelca, DNA minor-groove binder + CYP3A4 + 99% PPB; confirmed NOT OATP1B1 substrate per label), dotinurad (oral 2020 Japan / 2024 China URAT1 inhibitor, multi-UGT substrate 1A1/1A3/1A9/2B7; Liu 2025 China HV SAD), belinostat (IV 2014 NME Beleodaq, UGT1A1-dominant fm~80-90% HDAC inhibitor; Wang 2013 PLOS One HCC patients Day-1 1200 mg/m²). Belinostat dose is supratherapeutic (1200 vs labeled 1000 mg/m²) -- only N=6 single-dose cohort; linear PK allows 1000/1200 back-scaling at scoring time.

paclitaxel.notes: OATP1B3 (primary) + OATP1B1 (secondary) substrate per Smith NF et al 2005 Chem Biol Interact 152:287–298; established in Leblanc et al 2018 DMD review as well. Paclitaxel is solubilized in Cremophor EL, which itself perturbs PK nonlinearly; the FDA label Cmax reflects the clinically administered Cremophor-containing product (i.e., Taxol, not nab-paclitaxel Abraxane). Mean Cmax 3650 ng/mL = 3.65 mg/L. SD not provided by the label — arithmetic mean only, consistent with rifampin entry precedent. Cross-study interstudy median from Vion 2023 systematic review (PMC8572663) Table 1 is 5.1 μM (= 4.35 mg/L at MW 853.9) [IQR 4.5–5.7 μM = 3.84–4.87 mg/L] across n=18 studies, reassuringly close to label value. Nonlinear PK: Cmax increases supra-proportionally with dose (Gianni 1995 JCO 13:180–190). AAFE-interpretation caveat: engine Cmax prediction may over/under estimate depending on whether nonlinear saturation is modeled.

zibotentan.notes: AstraZeneca endothelin A receptor antagonist (ZD4054). Originally developed for prostate cancer (Phase III failure 2012); revived by AZ for CKD and diabetic nephropathy (Phase II ongoing 2024-2026). Included as non-NME drug with 2024 primary HV PK publication. Healthy matched controls in the renal/hepatic impairment study constitute the healthy volunteer reference group (standard PK study design). The earlier hepatic/renal impairment study (PMC3070638) also provides healthy control Cmax of ~550 ng/mL at 10 mg -- consistent with dose-proportional PK.
